payload.rebuttal: argued: Criterion 5's claim is about the GATE line's rendered text: 'gates: attempt N, K new failures -> decision', with a failing gate named on no GATE line. That text comes from describe()'s branch `if event.new_failures is not None and event.decision is not None: return f"gates: attempt {attempt}, {new_failures} new failures -> {decision}"`, which never reads event.gates. The spec requires that branch stay untouched: 'The GATE line keeps its exact text. Criterion 5 holds it... Leave the rendered text alone.' So no value of the names expression on a GATE-phase Attempt, correct or swapped, can change what the golden fixture renders. That insensitivity is a property of the existing renderer, not a gap in my diff, and I cannot fix it without making the GATE line depend on .gates, which would itself violate criterion 5. The swapped condition is a real bug: it would stop REBUT lines from naming gates at all and wrongly populate .gates on GATE-phase events. It is caught, just not by criterion 5's own declared witness. All three new tests I added for criteria 1-3 (test_a_green_rebuttal_re_run_logs_each_gate_result_against_the_rebuttal, test_a_red_rebuttal_line_names_each_gate_that_failed_anew, test_an_errored_or_drifted_rebuttal_re_run_logs_each_gate_with_no_count) assert on Attempt.gates and on the REBUT line's rendered text, and each fails under this exact swap. The host's probe found no failing test because a criterion probe is checked only against its own criterion's declared witness, and criterion 5's declared witness is test_watch_output_matches_the_golden_fixture alone, a mapping fixed by the task's own witness list. I cannot edit tests/test_events.py (forbidden) or change the GATE line's rendering (out of scope, and would break criterion 5 itself), so there is no permitted code change that closes this. The underlying behavior is already guarded by this spec's own new witnesses.
